doc.title: Chuck Findley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 6, 2023

title: Competition, personalities and fun in the section
summary: Rowe asks about competition; Findley says performance and personality decided calls and most players were happy.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: It sounds like you’re describing a situation that there was so much work and so many good musicians but it was not competitive. Like how come they called that guy for this gig instead of me but that wasn’t a necessary thing that happened at the time.
It did — it did happen but it was only because of the performance. And personalities had a lot to do with it as well I think. You know there were some people that were, once again

no names, but that were not the nicest, you know, person to have in the band. But in general I’d say 90 percent of them or more were wonderful, happy people. You know and like I said that happiness comes out through that piece of brass that you have in your hands. And what you hear Sweets play, Sweets had a signature — oh he was funny too, very funny I mean so we’d tell jokes and lines and things. Well I mean if anything the leader would have to tell us, “Hey come on guys, be a little quiet here” you know because we were having too much fun. But it came out on the record, the beauty of having fun through music. And that’s the way I always grew up and when I played I always had fun.
